title: Copilot Money Alternatives 2026: Plans and Pricing
h1: Copilot Money Alternatives 2026: Plans and Pricing Compared
metaDescription: Copilot Money alternatives compared: Monarch, YNAB, Simplifi, Tiller, and EveryDollar, with published plan prices, trials, and budgeting methods.
intro:
Monarch, YNAB, Simplifi, Tiller and EveryDollar are five Copilot Money alternatives with published pricing and distinct budgeting methods. Published prices run from a free EveryDollar tier to $17.99 a month on EveryDollar Premium monthly billing, and each option differs in platform availability, trial duration and sharing rules. At The Modern Wallet, we compare published subscription costs and feature limits so households can assess their software expenses before paying.

[Copilot Money](https://www.copilot.money) is $109 billed yearly (limited-time, listed instead of $119); the page shows $9 per month as the yearly-billing equivalent and publishes no monthly-billing price. Copilot Money provides one plan with no tiers, no add-ons and no Artificial Intelligence (AI) credits, covering connections to over 16,000 banks, a money assistant and customer support from real humans. Its pricing page lists access for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web, while its Households sharing feature is marked as coming soon.

For context on the broader market, explore our [best budgeting apps roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps/) and our [best net worth tracker roundup](/roundup/best-net-worth-tracker/). If you want to evaluate specific competing products in depth, read our [Monarch alternatives](/alternatives/monarch-money/) guide, our [YNAB alternatives](/alternatives/ynab/) breakdown, or our [guide to making a budget](/guides/how-to-make-a-budget/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Copilot Money Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting an alternative to Copilot Money comes down to five operational points: device platforms, household collaboration, budgeting methodology, trial length, and annual commitment.

First, review platform availability. Copilot Money's pricing page lists access strictly on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web. 

Second, determine whether you need to share access today. Copilot Money marks its Households sharing feature as coming soon on its pricing page. YNAB allows a single subscription to be shared among up to six people at no extra cost. Simplifi includes sharing with one other person. 

Third, match the budgeting philosophy to your habits. Copilot Money tracks transactions and balances with an automated money assistant. YNAB relies on the YNAB Method, asking users what each dollar is for before spending it. EveryDollar uses a method where users give every dollar a job. Simplifi sets up a Spending Plan that isolates bills and savings first, leaving the remainder for day-to-day spending. Tiller syncs accounts into private spreadsheets you own.

Fourth, check the risk-free evaluation terms. Copilot Money does not list a standard free trial duration on its main pricing table. In contrast, YNAB provides a 34-day free trial with no credit card required when signing up directly on its website. Tiller offers a 30-day trial where the card is not charged until the period ends, paired with a subsequent 30-day refund window that yields up to 60 days risk-free. Monarch offers a free first week with a money-back guarantee. EveryDollar provides a 14-day free trial for its Premium plan.

Fifth, compare total subscription costs over a full year. Copilot Money lists an annual price of $109 (listed instead of $119 as a limited-time offer). Monarch Core costs $99.99 per year, while YNAB costs $109 per year. Tiller charges $99 per year. EveryDollar Premium costs $79.99 billed annually. These fixed annual figures allow direct comparison across budgeting budgets.

alternatives.heading: Monarch Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Monarch sells two subscription plans: Core at $99.99 per year or $14.99 per month, and Plus at $199.99 per year. Monarch offers a free first week, allows cancellation at any time, and provides a money-back guarantee. A promotional banner on Monarch's pricing page advertises 30% off Core for one year when using code WELCOME, subject to terms and expiration. Monarch states that it displays no advertisements, never sells customer financial data, and recommends completing sign-up on the web rather than through mobile app stores.

 Monarch Plus adds forecasting tools, tracking for multiple income sources such as a small business, and deeper investment tracking features.

Monarch fits users who want multi-income business tracking and forecasting tools without advertisements.

Versus Copilot Money, Monarch costs less on an annual Core plan. Copilot Money lists $109 billed yearly (marked instead of $119), showing $9 per month on that yearly view. Monarch Core costs $14.99 per month, which totals $179.88 across 12 monthly payments. Comparing annual plans, Monarch Core at $99.99 is $9.01 cheaper per year than Copilot Money at $109. However, upgrading to Monarch Plus at $199.99 per year costs $90.99 more than Copilot Money's $109 annual rate. Copilot Money includes a money assistant on its single plan.

alternatives.heading: YNAB Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
YNAB (You Need A Budget) provides a proactive budgeting system with two billing options. Its Annual plan costs $109 paid annually, which equals $9.08 per month and is advertised as saving $70 compared to monthly billing. Its Monthly plan costs $14.99 per month. All prices are listed in United States (US) dollars plus applicable sales tax. YNAB includes a 34-day free trial that requires no credit card when signing up directly on the YNAB website, though app store sign-ups may require payment details. College students get a free 365-day trial. A single YNAB subscription can be shared with a group of up to six people at no additional charge.

The YNAB Method asks what each dollar is for. YNAB includes debt tools with an integrated loan calculator.

YNAB fits budgeters who follow the YNAB Method and households that want to share one subscription across up to six individuals.

Versus Copilot Money, YNAB charges the exact same annual price of $109, while offering broader multi-user sharing. Copilot Money's pricing page lists Households as coming soon, whereas YNAB already supports sharing with up to six people under its standard subscription. On monthly billing, YNAB costs $14.99 per month ($179.88 over 12 months), which is $70.88 more than its $109 annual rate. Copilot Money includes a money assistant on its single plan.

alternatives.heading: Simplifi Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Simplifi is a cloud budgeting application for web and mobile devices, developed by Quicken. The Simplifi homepage displays pricing figures of $3.99 per month and $6.99 labeled billed annually. A footnote explains that discounts are calculated on the annual price, the final price paid may differ from the monthly figure multiplied by 12, promotional offers apply only to the first year for new memberships ordered directly by December 8, 2026, and subscriptions renew automatically at the then-current standard rates. Simplifi states that its services are not designed to function outside the US and Canada.

Simplifi connects to over 14,000 financial institutions. Its feature set includes a Spending Plan (bills and savings first, remainder to spend), Projected Cash Flow up to 12 months ahead, net worth tracking, Watchlist, Savings Goals, a Retirement Planner, Quicken AI, free one-on-one setup help, and the ability to share with one other person.

Simplifi fits individuals and couples who want forward-looking cash flow projections, retirement planning tools, and free one-on-one setup help.

Versus Copilot Money, Simplifi offers forward-looking cash flow projections up to 12 months ahead and active two-person sharing, whereas Copilot Money lists Households as coming soon.

alternatives.heading: Tiller Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
Tiller is a personal finance service that syncs accounts into private spreadsheets you own. Tiller offers a 30-day free trial, followed by an annual subscription price of $99 per year, with sales tax added where required by law. Tiller states that its service carries no advertisements and no hidden fees. New subscribers register using a Microsoft or Google account, and credit cards are not charged until the initial 30-day trial concludes. Tiller pairs this with an additional 30-day money-back refund guarantee, providing up to 60 days of risk-free evaluation.

Tiller syncs accounts into private spreadsheets using a Microsoft or Google account. 

Tiller fits spreadsheet users who want account data synced into Google Sheets or Microsoft spreadsheets.

Versus Copilot Money, Tiller costs $99 per year, which is $10 less than Copilot Money's $109 annual rate. On a monthly equivalent basis, Tiller's $99 annual fee equals $8.25 per month, compared to the $9 monthly equivalent shown on Copilot Money's annual plan. Tiller's pricing page lists no money assistant, whereas Copilot Money includes one on its single plan.

alternatives.heading: EveryDollar Pricing, Plans and Fit
alternatives.body:
EveryDollar, developed by Ramsey Solutions, is a budgeting application built around giving every dollar a job. EveryDollar offers a permanent Free version that includes monthly budget creation, unlimited budget categories, manual transaction entry, sinking funds, split transactions, and tracking for bill due dates.

EveryDollar Premium adds automated bank connectivity, custom budget reports, Comma-Separated Values (CSV) transaction exports, coach Question and Answer (Q&A), and net worth projection modeling. Following a 14-day free trial, EveryDollar Premium costs $79.99 billed annually (listed as $6.67 per month equivalent), or $17.99 per month when billed on a monthly basis.

EveryDollar fits people who want to give every dollar a job with a free manual option, or those who value coach Q&A on the Premium plan.

Versus Copilot Money, EveryDollar provides a free tier for manual budget tracking. For automated bank syncing, EveryDollar Premium billed annually costs $79.99 per year, saving $29.01 compared to Copilot Money's $109 annual price. On monthly billing, EveryDollar Premium costs $17.99 per month ($215.88 over 12 months), compared to $79.99 billed annually. Copilot Money includes a money assistant and bank connections on its single plan.

alternatives.heading: Who This Is Not For
alternatives.body: Copilot Money lists platform availability for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web, with Households sharing marked as coming soon. YNAB allows one subscription to be shared among up to six people, while Simplifi supports sharing with one other person. EveryDollar provides a free tier with manual transaction entry, while automated bank connections require its Premium tier. Monarch Core and Tiller offer annual plans starting at $99.99 and $99 per year respectively.

alternatives.heading: What Would Change Our Answer on Copilot Money Alternatives
alternatives.body:
The analysis on this page is based on published prices, features, and platform limits checked on November 24, 2026. Several potential moves by these providers would shift the cost calculations and recommendations:

If Copilot Money releases its Households sharing feature without adding an extra fee, its value for partners and families would rise relative to YNAB.

If Copilot Money removes its limited-time $109 annual pricing listed instead of $119, the comparative annual math against Monarch and YNAB would shift.

If Monarch alters its Core ($99.99) or Plus ($199.99) pricing tiers, or makes its WELCOME promo code permanent, the comparative annual math would adjust accordingly.

If YNAB modifies its 34-day free trial or changes its policy allowing up to six people to share one $109 subscription, the multi-user cost advantage would shift.

If Simplifi alters the pricing or expiration date on its promotional first-year offer of $3.99 per month, or renews at then-current rates, the cost comparison against Copilot Money's flat annual fee would change.

If EveryDollar adjusts its $79.99 annual or $17.99 monthly Premium pricing, the threshold at which its automated tier beats Copilot Money would move.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Copilot Money Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Copilot Money fits individuals on Apple devices or the Web who want a single-tier subscription without upsells or feature tiers. Copilot Money costs $109 billed yearly (marked instead of $119), providing access to all features with no tiers, no add-ons, and no AI credits.

Copilot Money connects to over 16,000 financial institutions, includes a money assistant, and provides customer support from real humans. Its pricing page specifies access across iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web. Copilot Money also explicitly states that it never sells customer financial data.

For solo users who prefer a money assistant, Copilot Money includes one with its single plan. If you do not need immediate multi-user sharing and use Apple devices or the Web, Copilot Money provides that exact environment.

verdict:
Copilot Money costs $109 billed yearly for a single plan with a money assistant and bank syncing across iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web. Monarch offers multi-income business tracking starting at $99.99 per year. YNAB delivers a budgeting method asking what each dollar is for with sharing for up to six people for $109 per year. Simplifi provides 12-month projected cash flow, Tiller automates private spreadsheets for $99 per year, and EveryDollar maintains a free manual budgeting tier alongside a $79.99 annual Premium plan.

To choose the right alternative, determine whether you need partner sharing today, identify your preferred device platforms, and compare the annual subscription prices in the table above.

faqs.question: What should I use instead of Copilot Money for budgeting?
faqs.answer: Monarch, YNAB, Simplifi, Tiller and EveryDollar are the five primary alternatives to Copilot Money. Monarch offers forecasting tools, Simplifi offers cash flow and net worth tracking, YNAB and EveryDollar provide distinct budgeting methods, and Tiller syncs bank data directly into private spreadsheets.

faqs.question: How much does Copilot Money cost?
faqs.answer: Copilot Money costs $109 billed yearly under a limited-time offer listed instead of $119, with the page showing $9 per month on that annual plan. It offers a single plan with no tiers, no add-ons, and no AI credits.

faqs.question: Is there a free alternative to Copilot Money?
faqs.answer: EveryDollar offers a free version that includes monthly budget creation, unlimited categories, manual transaction entry, split transactions, and bill due dates. However, automatic bank synchronization requires EveryDollar Premium.

faqs.question: Can you share a Copilot Money subscription with a partner?
faqs.answer: Copilot Money lists its Households sharing feature as coming soon on its pricing page. If you need immediate sharing, YNAB supports sharing with up to six people, while Simplifi allows sharing with one other person.

faqs.question: Does Copilot Money offer an Android app?
faqs.answer: Copilot Money's pricing page lists platform availability for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Web. It does not list Android on its pricing page.
